appended_meaning:
The materially referenced transfer and reprogramming controls are compared at complete section 512 and section 514(a)-(b) in PL113-235 division G 2015, PL115-31 division H 2017, PL116-94 division A 2020 and PL117-328 division H 2023. The established section 3 rule keeps each this-Act reference within its own division unless expressly provided otherwise. The literal health-transfer reference chain, its dated periods/amendment scopes and earlier original-purpose/time and availability qualifications remain. No automatic current-year substitution, actual transfer or current-grant application is made.

Complete section 512 bars transfer of funds made available in the Act/division to a United States Government department, agency or instrumentality except pursuant to a transfer made by, or transfer authority provided in, that Act or any other appropriation Act. Both an enacted transfer and provided transfer authority remain within the exception, as does the any-other-appropriation-Act branch. This is not a ban on every authorized interagency transfer, a new free-standing transfer power or a determination that any particular other statute satisfies the printed exception. The already captured section 501 balance-transfer authority keeps its own corresponding-account/original-purpose/original-period constraints; no claimed transfer resets those constraints or decides current funding eligibility.

Complete 514(a) and (b) retain three covered-funding branches: funds provided under the Act/division; previous-appropriations funds for agencies funded by that Act that remain available for obligation or expenditure in its printed fiscal year; and Treasury-account funds derived from fee collections available to those agencies. The original printed fiscal years are 2015, 2017, 2020 and 2023 respectively, in both subsections. Prior available balances and fee-derived funding are not dropped or converted into all funds everywhere. Matching structural language does not erase those years, declare that every earlier period is now 2025 or establish actual balances or obligations.

Complete 514(a) addresses reprogramming that creates new programs; eliminates a program, project or activity; increases funds or personnel by any means for a project or activity whose funds have been denied or restricted; relocates offices or employees; reorganizes or renames offices; reorganizes programs or activities; or contracts out or privatizes functions or activities presently performed by Federal employees. All seven triggers remain. It conditions availability for obligation or expenditure through such reprogramming on the specified advance consultation and written notification. The separate subsection (b) monetary/percentage threshold is not imported into (a), and the condition is not changed into a permanent ban on all named activities or a finding that any agency carried them out.

Complete 514(b) separately addresses reprogramming in excess of $500,000 or 10 percent, whichever is less, that augments existing programs/projects including construction projects/activities; reduces by 10 percent funding for an existing program/project/activity or numbers of personnel by 10 percent as approved by Congress; or arises from general personnel-reduction savings that would change existing programs/activities/projects as approved by Congress. All three branches and the distinct personnel and funding reductions remain. In excess of is not changed to at least, whichever is less is not changed to the larger threshold, and the percentage branch or construction-project context is not removed. No actual reprogramming size, reduction, savings or prior congressional approval is found.

Both subsections require consultation with the House and Senate Appropriations Committees 15 days in advance of the reprogramming or an announcement of intent relating to it, whichever occurs earlier, and written notification to those Committees 10 days in advance of the reprogramming. The earlier-announcement consultation trigger and the separate actual-reprogramming written-notification deadline remain distinct. Consultation is not rewritten as notification alone, the 10-day requirement is not substituted for the 15-day requirement, and no new requirement to obtain committee approval is invented. No actual consultation, announcement, notification, compliance or violation is inferred.

The four section 512 clauses match at the complete operative extent. The four complete 514 clauses share the compared operative structure with their distinct printed source fiscal years retained. Private comparison removes notes/page markers and substitutes each verified source-year token only in the comparison, after checking its two occurrences; canonical original text is unchanged. Dates, glyphs, annotations, page markers and division identities remain distinct. This bounded comparison does not decide all current carry-forward, other-transfer-authority or individual grant applications. It remains member-neutral context for whole H.R. 1968 passage, without a separate transfer/reprogramming policy stance or four additional legislative actions. Shared compacts, recorded choices, counting, eligibility, prior needle-program version differences and the compiled proposition graph remain unchanged.

This completes only the selected transfer/reprogramming controls. Other materially relevant program, HHS and general requirements, substantive cross-references, actual current funding/application and remaining package authorities remain executable research. Unfinished research is not unavailable evidence. All 70 separate application questions, including frozen Q68/Q69/Q70, remain unchanged. No full conditions/fund/package/domain closure, independent acceptance, production eligibility or publication is declared.

Sec. 512. None of the funds made available in this Act may be transferred to any department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States Government, except pursuant to a transfer made by, or transfer authority provided in, this Act or any other appropriation Act. 

Sec. 514. (a) None of the funds provided under this Act, or provided under previous appropriations Acts to the agencies funded by this Act that remain available for obligation or expenditure in fiscal year 2015, or provided from any accounts in the Treasury of the United States derived by the collection of fees available to the agencies funded by this Act, shall be available for obligation or expenditure through a reprogramming of funds that-- (1) creates new programs; (2) eliminates a program, project, or activity; (3) increases funds or personnel by any means for any project or activity for which funds have been denied or restricted; [[Page 128 STAT. 2517]] (4) relocates an office or employees; (5) reorganizes or renames offices; (6) reorganizes programs or activities; or (7) contracts out or privatizes any functions or activities presently performed by Federal employees; unless the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate are consulted 15 days in advance of such reprogramming or of an announcement of intent relating to such reprogramming, whichever occurs earlier, and are notified in writing 10 days in advance of such reprogramming. (b) None of the funds provided under this Act, or provided under previous appropriations Acts to the agencies funded by this Act that remain available for obligation or expenditure in fiscal year 2015, or provided from any accounts in the Treasury of the United States derived by the collection of fees available to the agencies funded by this Act, shall be available for obligation or expenditure through a reprogramming of funds in excess of $500,000 or 10 percent, whichever is less, that-- (1) augments existing programs, projects (including construction projects), or activities; (2) reduces by 10 percent funding for any existing program, project, or activity, or numbers of personnel by 10 percent as approved by Congress; or (3) results from any general savings from a reduction in personnel which would result in a change in existing programs, activities, or projects as approved by Congress; unless the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate are consulted 15 days in advance of such reprogramming or of an announcement of intent relating to such reprogramming, whichever occurs earlier, and are notified in writing 10 days in advance of such reprogramming.

Sec. 506. (a) None of the funds appropriated in this Act, and none of the funds in any trust fund to which funds are appropriated in this Act, shall be expended for any abortion.
